program_name: Bachelor in Communication Sciences and Culture (IT: Laurea in Scienze della Comunicazione e Cultura; DE: Bachelor in Kommunikations- und Kulturwissenschaften). Faculty of Education, Free University of Bozen-Bolzano (unibz). Degree course director: Prof. Alessandro Vietti. Note on naming: unibz's own marketing copy on the programme page and in the brochure still calls it 'the study programme in Media, Communication and Culture' in the 'Course structure' and 'Career opportunities' sections — this is legacy wording, not a second programme. The official name in all administrative documents (admission-information PDF, ranking-list decrees, study plan) is 'Bachelor in Communication Sciences and Culture'.
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The 'At a glance' box states verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. The admission-information PDF states: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' WEIGHTING (derived by counting the language tag on every core module in the published 2026/27 Course Offering for students 'Enrolled from 2025', which currently covers years 1-2 only, 108 CP of core teaching): ITALIAN 48 CP (~44%) — Introduction to Linguistics, Social Statistics, Sociolinguistics, Sociology of Economic and Work Processes, Media Ecology, Techniques of Visual Communication + Music as Communication (12), Sociology of Culture; ENGLISH 36 CP (~33%) — Marketing and Communication, Cultural Studies, Computer-Mediated Communication, Virtual Communication, Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology of Communication; GERMAN 24 CP (~22%) — Theories of Communication, Language and Media Communication, Anthropology of Intercultural Processes, Principles of Sociology. So the language mix is ITALIAN-DOMINANT, with English a clear second and German the smallest share. This is materially different from the marketing framing of three equal languages. One 12-CP module (Theories of Communication and Cultural Studies) is deliberately split across two languages: Theories of Communication in German, Cultural Studies in English. Third-year modules are not yet listed in the 'Enrolled from 2025' offering, so the full-degree ratio may shift. [uncertain]
campus: Brixen-Bressanone (the Faculty of Education campus, NOT the Bozen-Bolzano main campus). Faculty of Education Secretariat: Regensburger Allee 16 / viale Ratisbona 16, 39042 Brixen-Bressanone, Italy; Tel +39 0472 014000; faculty.education@unibz.it. The admission interview is also physically held in Brixen-Bressanone. Practical note for applicants: the central Advisory Service that handles applications sits at the Bozen-Bolzano campus (Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Tel +39 0471 012100, apply@unibz.it), so application questions and campus life are split across two towns roughly 40 km apart. 24/7 emergency line for the Brixen-Bressanone and Bruneck-Brunico campuses: +39 0472 011777.
degree_class: L-20 (Scienze della comunicazione / Communication Sciences). 180 ECTS, 3 years. The admission-information PDF confirms the national dual-enrolment rule applies with this class as the constraint: 'simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., L-18/L-18 and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents)'.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered, actively recruiting, and STILL OPEN as of the verification date. All three application sessions ran: the Early Bird and Late ranking lists have been published and signed, and the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026) was explicitly opened for this programme because places remained unfilled. The unibz additional-session page lists the programme with the marker 'Application possible'. As of 2026-08-29 the Additional Session application window is OPEN and closes 04/09/2026 at noon local time — this is the last chance to enter the 2026/27 cohort, and it is open to EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only. Evidence of under-subscription: only 20 EU applicants were admitted in Early Bird against 30 places, and only 9 in the Late session against 10 places — 29 admitted against 40 EU places overall. The 2027/28 academic year already appears as a selectable year in the course-offering catalogue, so the programme is not being phased out.
is_new_programme: No — this is a long-established programme, not a new one. A 'Manifesto degli studi' for the L-20 Corso di Laurea in Scienze della Comunicazione e Cultura exists from 2019, and signed unibz ranking-list decrees for the programme exist from 2020, so it has been running for at least the better part of a decade. HOWEVER, the STUDY PLAN was revised recently: the faculty publishes two distinct course catalogues, 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' and 'Course Offering - enrolled before 2025', which means a new study plan took effect for the cohort entering in 2025/26. Applicants for 2026/27 follow the newer 'from 2025' plan. The exact original launch year of the programme is not stated on any unibz page consulted. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: NO majors and NO tracks — there is a single study plan for all students, unlike Design and Art (two majors) or Industrial Mechanical Engineering (five study plans). Structure (180 CP): 1st year — Introduction to Linguistics 6, Principles of Sociology 6, Techniques of Visual Communication and Music as Communication 12 (split 6+6), Social Statistics 6, Anthropology of Intercultural Processes 6, Psychology of Communication 6, Marketing and Communication 6, Computer-Mediated Communication 6, Optional Subjects 6. 2nd year — Sociolinguistics 6, Theories of Communication and Cultural Studies 12 (split 6+6), Sociology of Culture 6, Virtual Communication and Human-Computer Interaction 12 (split 6+6), Sociology of Economic and Work Processes 6, Media Ecology 6, Language and Media Communication 6, Optional Subjects 6. 3rd year — Communication in Campaigns and Culture and Aesthetics 12 (split 6+6), Social Sustainability through Innovation 6, Statistics and Communication 6, Media Law 6, Organisational Communication 6, Internship 12, Final Exam 12. THE REAL FLEXIBILITY IS THE 12 OPEN CREDITS: the brochure states these are 'credits that you can obtain through optional modules and workshops offered within the programme or in other Faculties', letting a student lean the degree towards Economics, Visual Arts or New Technologies. COMPULSORY INTERNSHIP of minimum 300 hours (12 CP), chosen from unibz's partner network in Italy and abroad; optional and post-graduate internships also available. TWO PLAN VERSIONS coexist administratively ('Enrolled from 2025' vs 'enrolled before 2025') — 2026/27 entrants take the 'from 2025' plan. PART-TIME ENROLMENT is offered as a separate variant: it reduces the annual course load while keeping full access to university services, and — importantly — it is chosen AFTER enrolment (in October), not during the application. Exchange partners: LMU Munich, Lüneburg University, University of Koblenz-Landau (Germany), University of Malta, Universidad Complutense de Madrid.
english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for a candidate who speaks only English. This is one of the hardest unibz programmes for an English-only applicant, and harder than most trilingual degrees at the university, for three compounding reasons. (1) ENTRY BAR: the entry requirement is B2 in the FIRST language AND B2 in the SECOND language, with the PDF stating that failure means 'you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. An English-only candidate can certify English at B2/C1 but has no second language at B2, so the application is rejected before scoring. Note this is a full step above the more forgiving B2/B1 pattern used by, for example, Food and Enogastronomy Sciences. (2) THE SELECTION ITSELF IS BILINGUAL: 'The admission interview will be held in two of the three teaching languages chosen by the applicant.' The interview is worth 70 of the 90 available points, so even hypothetically getting past the paperwork, an English-only candidate cannot perform the assessment that decides admission. (3) EXIT BAR: graduation demands C1 in the first language, C1 in the SECOND language and B2 in the third — the joint-highest exit requirement among unibz bachelors, and the degree cannot be awarded without it. On top of that, the actual teaching is Italian-dominant (48 CP Italian vs 36 CP English in the published years 1-2 offering) and B1 in the third language is required from the second semester of year one just to sit exams in that language. PRACTICAL VERDICT for a Turkish or other international applicant: this degree is only realistic for someone who already has, or can certify before the application deadline, B2 in Italian or German in addition to English. It should not be presented to English-only candidates as an option. The only mitigation unibz offers — free Language Centre courses and the September intensive course — applies to the THIRD language after admission, not to the second-language B2 needed to be admitted at all.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / limited places) with a merit ranking list, decided by a MANDATORY ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW plus documentary scoring. There is no open access. Concretely it is: interview (70 pts) + academic/extracurricular titles (10 pts) + certified third-language level (10 pts) = 90 points maximum. NOT applicable to this programme: TOLC, CENT-S, SAT, any written entrance exam, any portfolio, any motivation letter, any project proposal, any video submission. Three admission sessions exist for EU/parity applicants (Early Bird, Late, Additional); non-EU applicants living abroad get ONE session only. Separate ranking lists are drawn for EU/parity applicants and for non-EU applicants living abroad.
academic_requirements: One of the following qualifications is required: (a) a secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system; or (b) an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. Verbatim on equivalence: 'Foreign school leaving certificates are considered equivalent if obtained after 12 years of education. In this case, you furthermore must have attended at least the last two years in the foreign school system (e.g. Irish Leaving Certificate: it is not enough to attend one year and obtain the foreign certificate).' The 12-year rule plus the two-year attendance rule is the operative filter for international applicants — a Turkish lise diploması (12 years) satisfies the duration test provided the last two years were actually attended in that system. Additional national-level constraint: 'The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research has set specific admission requirements for holders of certain certificates (e.g. American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates)' — holders of those must contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service) before applying, because a bare US high school diploma or a small number of A-Levels is typically insufficient without supplementary evidence. There is NO minimum grade average, NO required subject combination, NO mathematics prerequisite and NO ECTS/SSD requirement (SSD codes are a master-level concept and do not apply to this bachelor). Language requirements are a separate and eliminatory condition: 'To be admitted, you must fulfil the language requirements indicated in the section "Language requirements".' Dual-enrolment: a maximum of 2 programmes simultaneously, not in the same degree class and differing by at least 2/3 of course content.
entry_exam_or_test: NO written entrance examination of any kind. The list of tests that do NOT apply: no unibz written admission exam, no TOLC-I or any other TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no subject test, no logic/aptitude test. The single assessment is an ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW (see the 'interview' field), scored out of 70 of the 90 total points. Interview dates by session: Early Bird 13/05/2026; Late 14/07/2026; Additional Session 15/09/2026. The only other examinations connected with admission are the unibz LANGUAGE CENTRE PROFICIENCY EXAMS, which are not selection tests but one of four ways to prove the required language levels — Early Bird: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). CRITICAL GAP: NO language exam dates are published for the Additional Application Session. Anyone applying in the currently open Additional window (18/08 - 04/09/2026) must therefore already hold recognised certificates or qualify through the school/degree medium-of-instruction routes — there is no unibz exam left to sit. A further restriction applies to the Language Centre route for this programme: 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams.'
selection_scoring: Maximum 90 points, in three components, applied identically in all three sessions. (1) ADMISSION INTERVIEW ON GENERAL KNOWLEDGE — max 70 points (78% of the total, so the interview effectively IS the admission decision). (2) EVALUATION OF OTHER ACADEMIC AND/OR EXTRACURRICULAR TITLES — max 10 points, only where 'with relevance for the course'. (3) KNOWLEDGE OF THE THIRD OFFICIAL TEACHING LANGUAGE — max 10 points, on a published and unusually non-linear scale: 'A2 = 1 point; B1 = 2 points; B2 = 3 points; C1 = 4 points; C2 = 10 points'. Note the sharp jump from C1 (4 points) to C2 (10 points) — a near-native third language is worth 2.5x a C1, while the whole A2-to-C1 range is worth almost nothing; this rewards genuine trilingual candidates and gives very little to someone who merely dabbled. Only certificates recognised by the unibz Language Centre, or exams taken at the Language Centre, count for these points. TIE-BREAK: 'If scores are equal, the younger applicant will have priority.' NO MINIMUM PASSING SCORE is published anywhere for this programme — unlike Design (42/100), Critical Creative Practices (60/100), EMMA (55/95) or Entrepreneurship (70/100). The only numerical threshold published is the OFA trigger: fewer than 12 out of 24 points on the text-comprehension criteria within the interview (see 'ofa_rules'), which implies the interview is internally sub-scored with a 24-point text-comprehension block inside the 70. The published ranking lists give only ranks and applicant IDs, never scores, so no historical cut-off can be reconstructed. COMPETITIVENESS IN PRACTICE: with 20 EU admitted against 30 Early Bird places and 9 against 10 Late places, the programme did not fill its quota, so in 2026/27 admission was in practice about clearing the language bar and performing acceptably at interview rather than beating a competitive cut-off. [uncertain]
bonus_points: NO bonus-point scheme in the sense used elsewhere at unibz. Specifically absent: no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is a Software Engineering / Computing for Data Science device and applies only to master applicants), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), no start-up project presentation bonus (Entrepreneurship). The rubric is closed at 90 points. The two components that function like bonuses within that closed rubric are (a) the max 10 points for 'other academic and/or extracurricular titles with relevance for the course' — the only place where olympiads, media/journalism work, volunteering, published writing, communication-related courses or comparable achievements can be credited, and (b) the max 10 points for the certified third-language level (A2=1, B1=2, B2=3, C1=4, C2=10). The C2 jump to 10 points is the single largest discretionary gain available to an applicant outside the interview itself.
portfolio_and_materials: NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video, NO project proposal, NO CV requirement and NO reference letters. None of unibz's usual creative-programme format limits (20 MB PDF portfolio, 2 A4 project proposal, 6,000-character motivation letter, 2-minute video) apply here — those belong to Design/Art and to certain masters. The only materials that carry score are the documents evidencing 'other academic and/or extracurricular titles' (max 10 points) and the language certificates evidencing the third-language level (max 10 points), both uploaded in the application portal. unibz publishes no file-format, page-count or size limit for the titles upload for this programme, and no template. HARD PROCEDURAL RULE: 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline' — nothing sent later, and nothing brought to the interview, is scored. Also: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified.' The only material with a stated exception route is language certificates, which 'if you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'. [uncertain]
interview: YES — a compulsory oral admission interview, and it is the decisive element of the whole procedure (70 of 90 points). FORMAT, verbatim: 'You have approximately 10-15 minutes time to read a newspaper article (taken from one of the major national and international newspapers and weekly news magazines), which will subsequently be discussed with the Admission Commission. The article concerns a subject regarding culture and communication.' So it is a live comprehend-and-discuss exercise on unseen current-affairs text, not a CV or motivation interview — there is no way to pre-prepare answers, and preparation means reading quality press on culture and communication regularly in two of the three languages. LANGUAGES: 'The admission interview will be held in two of the three teaching languages chosen by the applicant' — the applicant chooses which two, but two it must be. LOCATION: in person in Brixen-Bressanone; 'Location and time will be published on the website www.unibz.it.' REMOTE OPTION: video conference is possible only 'If you are unable to attend the interview appointment due to serious logistical difficulties', and requires 'a written and motivated request to the Faculty Secretariat at least 7 days before the date of the interview' — this is the route an overseas applicant must use, and the 7-day lead time is a hard deadline that is easy to miss. PUBLISHED 2026/27 INTERVIEW DATES: Early Bird 13/05/2026; Late 14/07/2026; Additional Session 15/09/2026. INTERNAL SUB-SCORING: the interview contains a text-comprehension block scored out of 24, and scoring under 12/24 triggers OFA. ADMISSION COMMISSION (as signed on the 2026/27 Early Bird ranking-list decree): chair Federica Viganò; members Alessandro Luigini, Andrea Abel, Daniela Salvucci, Alexander Glück, Evan Tedeschi.
conditional_admission: There is no explicitly named 'conditional admission' regime for this bachelor of the kind master programmes use (the '≥120 ECTS', or 140 for Data Analytics, rule is a master device and does not apply). What exists instead is the standard Italian arrangement for school-leavers who have not yet sat their final exam: they may apply and be ranked before graduating, and the qualification is produced later. Verbatim from the online-application section: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' The refund clause confirms the same logic from the other side: a candidate who pays the first instalment but does not enrol gets no refund 'unless you do not pass your secondary school final exam' — i.e. failing the maturità/final exam is the recognised way the place lapses without financial loss. A SEPARATE AND STRICTER RESERVE applies to non-EU applicants living abroad: the ranking-list decree states they are admitted WITH RESERVE ('ammessi e ammesse con riserva'), and the reserve is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. A further reserve applies to anyone with a foreign qualification who has not yet uploaded the ARDI/CIMEA paperwork: 'Until you have uploaded the documentation indicated above, you can only be admitted with reserve', and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' No 'late enrolment until 11/12/2026 if places remain' provision is published for this programme; its published enrolment windows close at 06/08/2026 (Early Bird and Late) and 25/09/2026 (Additional Session). [uncertain]
ofa_rules: YES — this programme assigns OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations), but on a basis unique among unibz bachelors: not a mathematics test (as with Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, or Tourism Sport and Event Management) but TEXT COMPREHENSION measured inside the admission interview. Verbatim: 'Additional learning requirements (OFA) are assigned to you if, during the admission process, you demonstrate a learning weakness in the area of understanding and summarizing the text presented during the interview (scoring less than 12 out of 24 points on the text comprehension criteria).' REMEDY: 'you must complete a 16-hour training program to acquire the specific knowledge and skills. The additional learning requirements (OFA) will be considered fulfilled upon passing, by the end of the first year of study, the exam administered at the conclusion of the training program.' CONSEQUENCE OF NOT CLEARING IT: 'If you do not fulfill the additional learning requirements by the end of the first year of study, you may enroll in the second year of study, but you will not be able to take exams for the second or third year of study until the OFA have been fully fulfilled' — enrolment continues but the degree effectively stalls, since no second- or third-year exams can be sat. The published ranking lists carry a footnote marking students who received OFA ('Persone a cui sono stati assegnati Obblighi Formativi Aggiuntivi (OFA)'), although no applicant on the 2026/27 Early Bird or Late lists is flagged in the extracted text. Practical implication for a non-native applicant: OFA risk is concentrated in exactly the skill the interview tests — reading and summarising a demanding newspaper article in a second language under time pressure.
language_requirements: This is the make-or-break field for the programme, and the requirement is eliminatory: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' ENTRY: 1st language B2, 2nd language B2, 3rd language no level required. IN-COURSE: from the second semester of the first year, B1 in the third language is the minimum to sit curricular examinations held in that language. EXIT: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 — the joint-strictest exit profile at unibz. Positions are defined by ability, not by which language it is: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (B2 or C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' PROOF: mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended from B1 for the 3rd. Uploaded in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or by registering under 'enrol for language exams', in both cases only after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. Administrative distinction: a final certificate from an ITALIAN public institution requires a self-declaration; one from a FOREIGN public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAM RESTRICTION specific to this programme: 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams' — B1 exams cannot be booked here, which matters because B2 is exactly the entry bar for the second language. SUPPORT AFTER ADMISSION (third language only): free Language Centre courses, a placement test for those without a third-language certificate, a three-week September intensive course for absolute beginners or anyone below B2, extensive courses of 4 h/week during semesters and intensive courses of 8 h/week between semesters, targeting 'B1 level by the end of the 1st year; B2 level by the end of the 2nd year'. WARNING: 'Beginner courses (A1) will be offered exclusively during the pre-semester intensive course session in September will no longer be offered during the academic year' — an absolute beginner who skips the September intensive has no A1 route later in the year.
entry_levels_by_position: B2 / B2 / none — 1st language B2, 2nd language B2, 3rd language no level required at entry. This is the STRICTER of the two common unibz trilingual patterns: it demands B2 in two languages, whereas the more accessible pattern (e.g. Food and Enogastronomy Sciences, Electronic and Information Engineering) asks only B2/B1. It is one notch below the hardest pattern (C1/B2, used by Public Policy and Accounting and Finance) but, because this is a bachelor aimed at school-leavers rather than graduates, the practical barrier is comparable. Positions are assigned by measured ability, not by the applicant's nationality or preference: the first language is whichever of German/Italian/English the applicant is strongest in, the third whichever they are weakest in. Failing the entry levels is not a deduction — it is exclusion from the admission procedure before scoring. From the 2nd semester of year one an additional in-course gate applies: B1 in the third language is required to sit examinations taught in that language.
exit_levels: C1 / C1 / B2 — first language C1, second language C1, third language B2, all on the Common European Framework of Reference. This is one step harder in the SECOND language than the common unibz exit profile of C1/B2/B2 (used, for example, by Food and Enogastronomy Sciences), and it directly gates graduation: the degree cannot be awarded until all three levels are met. Read together with the entry bar, a student must move from B2 to C1 in two languages and from zero (possible at entry) to B2 in the third over three years. The Language Centre supports only the third-language path with free courses targeting B1 by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2; closing the B2-to-C1 gap in the first and second languages is left to the student and to the trilingual teaching itself. Prospective applicants should treat this as the programme's real long-term risk: admission is winnable at B2/B2, but graduation requires genuine C1/C1/B2 trilingualism.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is required from the SECOND SEMESTER OF THE FIRST YEAR, verbatim: 'From the 2nd semester of the first year — 3rd language: a B1 level in the third language is a minimum requirement for taking the curricular examinations in that specific language.' The gate is language-specific, not global: a student below B1 in, say, German is blocked only from German-taught examinations, not from Italian- or English-taught ones. Given the published language split (German carries 24 CP of the core years 1-2, Italian 48 CP, English 36 CP), the size of the blocked block depends heavily on which language ends up third. The Language Centre's free-course targets are calibrated to this rule — B1 by the end of year 1, B2 by the end of year 2 — and a placement test is administered after admission to anyone who cannot certify the third language.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways, identical to the university-wide scheme. (1) THE MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH-SCHOOL YEAR, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian). For foreign qualifications: 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' (2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload their certificates and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if it is not stated on the degree itself. (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list; 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' (4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, booked online in the portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application. 2026/27 exam dates — Early Bird: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026); Additional Session: NONE PUBLISHED. Programme-specific limit on this route: 'you can only register for B2 level exams.' The PDF also warns: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' FIFTH ROUTE for foreign and bi-/multilingual schools: 'If the foreign language proficiency levels (for German, Italian, or English) are explicitly indicated on the diploma of graduation according to the Common European Framework of Reference (i.e., B1, B2 or C1), and if all four language abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) have been assessed, then the indicated levels will be accepted as a proof of proficiency for the second and/or third language' — upload the school-leaving certificate under the relevant language and the Language Centre decides on recognition. Note this route is explicitly limited to the SECOND and/or THIRD language, not the first.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026, 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants' (published trilingually as Beschluss des Universitätsrates / Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università / Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026). GENERAL CONDITIONS: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR skills and be issued by the certification provider itself; (2) it must show a sufficient result in every skill as an overall grade, or the detailed per-skill assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer. LEVEL DETERMINATION: where no overall result or level is shown, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed. NO COMPENSATION is accepted for failed parts and no averages are computed unless the certifying body itself provides them. NOT RECOGNISED: certificates obtained as remote 'home edition' exams (except those explicitly flagged in the list); single-skill attestations combined across different providers; certificates of attendance, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions; placement-test results; attestations issued by individual lecturers, lettori or teachers; and DAAD certificates. VALIDITY: an international language certificate must have been obtained within the last FIVE YEARS at the moment of submission, counted as whole calendar years from 1 January of the fifth preceding year and running through that entire year. Items listed under the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section have UNLIMITED validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf . Practical implication for this programme: because the lowest sub-skill governs, an IELTS or similar with one weak band drops the whole certificate below B2 and, since B2 is the entry bar for two languages, can cause outright exclusion rather than a lost point.
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment. unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalisation given in brackets. (1) EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time [2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 CEST]. (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only): 28/05 - 08/07/2026 by noon local time [2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08, 12:00 CEST]. (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only, opened at the Faculty's discretion when places remain): 18/08 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time [2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, 12:00 CEST]. STATUS AT THE VERIFICATION DATE (2026-08-29): sessions 1 and 2 are closed and their ranking lists are published; SESSION 3 IS OPEN, with six days left to the 04/09/2026 noon cut-off. unibz confirmed on its additional-session page that this programme is included, marked 'Application possible'. The Faculty's own caveat: 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places' — the Additional Session is never guaranteed in advance for a future intake. Re-application is permitted across sessions: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' Note also that language-exam registration periods are tied to the first two sessions only, so an Additional Session applicant must already hold acceptable proof of language level.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time [2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 CEST]. Verbatim: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' The Late Application and the Additional Application Session are both explicitly restricted to EU citizens, so for a Turkish, or any other non-EU, candidate living abroad the 2026/27 intake CLOSED ON 28/04/2026 and cannot be reopened — the currently open Additional Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026) is not available to them. The associated language-exam windows for this single session were 16/03/2026 and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026. A €50 non-refundable application fee applies to this group only. The next opportunity for a non-EU applicant living abroad is the 2027/28 Early Bird window, which by the pattern of recent years should open around early March 2027 (dates not yet published). THE ONE EXCEPTION: a non-EU citizen who already holds a qualifying Italian residence permit is treated as an EU applicant and does have access to the Late and Additional sessions — see 'parity_of_treatment'.
parity_of_treatment: Two groups are treated as EU applicants, and for a Turkish applicant this distinction is the single most consequential item in the whole admission process. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State'. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' THE PENALTY FOR GETTING THE UPLOAD WRONG IS SEVERE AND AUTOMATIC: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' Concretely, for 2026/27 that mis-step would have cost: access to the 40-place EU quota (dropping the applicant to the 4-place non-EU list), access to the Late session, access to the Additional session that is still open today, and it would have added the €50 fee, the Universitaly pre-enrolment step and the consulate-confirmed 'with reserve' admission. The same ranking-list decree restates the rule in Italian and German, confirming it is applied at the decree level and not merely as guidance. Also note the asymmetry created by the session structure: the parity route led to a window still open on 2026-08-29, whereas the non-EU-abroad route closed on 2026-04-28.
places_quotas: Three published numbers for 2026/27, identical in the programme page, the brochure and the admission-information PDF. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 30; Late Application 10 — 40 in total. NON-EU CITIZENS (LIVING ABROAD): Early Bird Application 4 (no Late, no Additional). The 'At a glance' summary compresses this to 'Places available: 40 EU + 4 non-EU'. CARRY-OVER RULE: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application' — unused Early Bird places roll forward, but only within the EU quota; unfilled non-EU places do not roll into the EU pool or into a later non-EU session. No separate quota is published for the Additional Session; it draws on whatever remains. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE, from the signed ranking-list decrees: Early Bird admitted 20 EU/parity candidates (against 30 places) and 1 non-EU candidate living abroad (against 4 places); the Late session admitted 9 EU candidates (against 10 places plus 10 carried over). Total 29 admitted against 40 EU places, which is why an Additional Session was opened. The 4-place non-EU quota is nominally tiny, but with only 1 admitted it was not the binding constraint in 2026/27 — the language requirement almost certainly was.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD: admission interviews 13/05/2026 [2026-05-13]; ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 [2026-05-27]; payment of the 1st instalment (€600, the payment that secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon [2026-06-05, 12:00]; enrolment from 10/07 to 06/08/2026 noon [2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06, 12:00]. LATE: interviews 14/07/2026 [2026-07-14]; ranking lists by 30/07/2026 [2026-07-30]; 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon [2026-08-06, 12:00]; enrolment 'from publication of the ranking list until 06/08/2026 (by noon local time)' — note the Late session compresses payment and enrolment onto the SAME deadline, leaving as little as a week between ranking publication and final enrolment. ADDITIONAL SESSION: interviews 15/09/2026 [2026-09-15]; ranking lists by 18/09/2026 [2026-09-18]; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon [2026-09-25, 12:00]; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 25/09/2026 noon — again payment and enrolment share one deadline, only three days after the list appears. MISSING EITHER DEADLINE IS FATAL AND AUTOMATIC: 'If you do not meet this deadline, you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted.' Paying does not make you a student: 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling. If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund unless you do not pass your secondary school final exam or, in the event of non-EU applicants living abroad, you do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in your country.' A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice. Related post-admission deadline from the Early Bird decree: applications for recognition of credits from previous university studies must be filed via the unibz Intranet by 18/09/2026.

Only B2-level exams can be booked for this programme, and no language-exam dates exist for the Additional Session. PREPARATORY AND START-OF-YEAR DATES: intensive language courses 01-18/09/2026 (Monday to Friday, 6 h/day) — the only chance in the year to take A1 beginner courses in the third language; Freshers Days 29-30/09/2026. ACADEMIC CALENDAR 2026/27: 1st semester classes 28/09-23/12/2026, holidays 24/12/2026-06/01/2027, classes resume 07-23/01/2027, exams 25/01-20/02/2027; 2nd semester classes 01/03-25/03/2027, holidays 26-29/03/2027, classes 30/03-12/06/2027, exams 14/06-10/07/2027; autumn exam session 23/08-25/09/2027. POST-ENROLMENT: part-time status is chosen in October, after enrolment, not at application; credit-recognition applications due via Intranet by 18/09/2026.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION, online via the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) an account, plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (2) the completed online form; (3) the attachments listed under 'Admission procedure', i.e. documentation of other academic and/or extracurricular titles relevant to the course (scored up to 10 points); (4) language certificates uploaded under 'upload language certificates' — mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended from B1 for the 3rd — and/or registration under 'enrol for language exams'; a certificate from an Italian public institution needs a self-declaration, one from a foreign public institution needs an uploaded scanned copy of the original; (5) the diploma of the qualification, if it was gained abroad and is already in hand (otherwise uploaded at enrolment); (6) for non-EU citizens claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay, plus a renewal request if it has expired. NOTE: there is NO 'study career' Excel template for this programme — that structured upload is a master-level requirement. NO portfolio, motivation letter, CV, video or project proposal is required. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements described under 'credential_recognition'. HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration'; 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline'; and 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' Transfers from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application at the start of the academic year; non-EU students must hand the residence permit in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. Verbatim: 'Application fee: € 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay) pay nothing to apply. The fee is separate from and additional to the €600 first tuition instalment that secures an admitted place.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are approximately €1,200 per academic year, in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which 'includes the revenue stamp of € 16' (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures an admitted place; 2nd instalment €600, which 'must be paid by March of the following year'. CONSEQUENCES: 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' NO REFUND if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (the health-authority certificate must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year); and foreign students holding a scholarship from the Italian government. REFUND: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' Fees reference pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's own admission-information PDF at https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-communication-sciences-and-culture_admission-information_en_GB.pdf . For budgeting, note that tuition is by far the smaller cost — unibz itself estimates at least €800/month of living costs in the Bozen-Bolzano area, and this programme is based in Brixen-Bressanone.
scholarships_grants: NO programme-specific scholarship is published for this degree — unlike Food and Enogastronomy Sciences, which has the Meran-Merano municipal awards. Only the university-wide and provincial routes apply. (1) PROVINCIAL STUDY GRANT from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, applied for through the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario: income-based, reported at between €1,680 and €6,960 per year; recipients also get a refund of their unibz tuition fees. The student associations sh.asus and MUA assist with the application. (2) MERIT SCHOLARSHIP after the first year, for students reaching an average grade of 27/30 — performance-based rather than means-tested. (3) MAE SCHOLARSHIPS funded by the Italian Ministero degli Affari Esteri, open to foreign students and Italian students living abroad; holders of an Italian government scholarship are additionally exempt from tuition fees. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS, verbatim: 'Non-EU citizens residing abroad cannot immediately apply for scholarships of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano. You will be able to apply only after one year of regular registered residence in South Tyrol.' In practice a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is ineligible for the provincial grant in year one, ineligible for the merit scholarship (which requires a completed first year), and left with only the MAE route or private funding — and, unlike some other unibz bachelors, has no programme-level award to fall back on. Reference page: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/studying-at-unibz . [uncertain]
credential_recognition: At enrolment, a holder of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the secondary school diploma plus an official translation into Italian — 'not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English'. Then, by education system: (a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN, INTERNATIONAL BACCALAUREATE, EUROPEAN BACCALAUREATE — Statement of CORRESPONDENCE, downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database – Italy. (b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — Statement of CORRESPONDENCE from ARDI *and* Statement of VERIFICATION issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence). (c) NON-EU COUNTRIES NOT SIGNATORY TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — Statement of COMPARABILITY issued by CIMEA *and* Statement of VERIFICATION issued by CIMEA. Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so a Turkish applicant falls under route (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification, plus an Italian translation of the diploma. ENFORCEMENT: 'Until you have uploaded the documentation indicated above, you can only be admitted with reserve'; 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents'; and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Underlying eligibility rules still apply on top of the paperwork: 12 years of education and at least the last two years attended in the foreign school system, with extra ministry conditions for American, British and Greek certificates. There is no ≥180 ECTS requirement — that is a master-level rule and does not apply to this bachelor. Because CIMEA and ARDI statements take weeks to obtain, they should be started well before the enrolment window, not after the ranking list appears.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for a non-EU citizen living abroad: apply to unibz in the EARLY BIRD window only (02/03 - 28/04/2026, €50 non-refundable fee) → sit the admission interview on 13/05/2026, in person in Brixen-Bressanone or by video conference if a written, motivated request reached the Faculty Secretariat at least 7 days earlier → appear on the SEPARATE non-EU ranking list (4 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/). Universitaly is MANDATORY: 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only'; the ranking-list decree adds that a missing Universitaly application makes the unibz application and enrolment void. PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC NUANCE: non-EU applicants living abroad are admitted WITH RESERVE, and the reserve is lifted only when the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. unibz warns explicitly that admission confers no right to a visa — 'the granting of a visa falls exclusively within the competence of embassies and consulates' — and that holding a study visa does not itself guarantee final enrolment. FINANCIAL MEANS FOR THE VISA: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area, excluding tuition; unibz states 'a bachelor programme will cost at least € 36,000, while a master programme will cost € 24,000' over the full course; health insurance and visa expenses come on top. AFTER ARRIVAL: 'By law, you will have to apply for a residence permit within 8 working days since your arrival in Italy' — contact the Advisory Service immediately on landing — and once the permesso di soggiorno is issued, a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. WORK LIMIT: 'no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year' on a study residence permit. REFUND EXCEPTION: a non-EU applicant abroad who pays the instalment but fails to obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities is entitled to a refund. SCHOLARSHIP TRAP: the provincial study grant requires one year of registered residence in South Tyrol, so it is unavailable in year one. Reference page: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/international/international-degree-seeking-applicants/degree-seeking-non-eu-citizens-living-abroad/

The admission-information PDF therefore functions as the operative call: it carries the quotas, the deadlines, the scoring rubric and the OFA rule. Two adjacent official documents that do exist: (a) the university-wide additional-application-session page, https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/additional-application-session/ , which is the formal notice opening the third session and lists this programme as 'Application possible'; and (b) the signed ranking-list decrees, which are administrative acts appealable to the Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days.
